hints: In right-angled triangle $DBC$, calculate $DB = AB - AD = 8 - 5 = 3$ cm and use $\tan\angle BDC = \frac{4}{3}$ to find the angle $\angle BDC$ in radians.
Since points $A, D, B$ lie on a straight line, find the sector angle $\angle ADC = \pi - \angle BDC$.
Calculate the arc length $s = r\theta = 5 \times \angle ADC$.
Calculate the length of chord $AC$ using Pythagoras in $\triangle ABC$: $AC = \sqrt{8^2 + 4^2}$, then sum the arc length and chord length for the perimeter.
walkthrough:
Find the length $DB$ and calculate the angle $\angle BDC$ in right-angled triangle $DBC$:
$$DB = AB - AD = 8 - 5 = 3\text{ cm}$$
$$\tan\angle BDC = \frac{BC}{DB} = \frac{4}{3} \implies \angle BDC = \arctan\left(\frac{4}{3}\right) \approx 0.92730\text{ rad}$$

Calculate the angle $\angle ADC$ of sector $DAC$ subtended at centre $D$:
$$\angle ADC = \pi - \angle BDC = \pi - 0.92730 \approx 2.21429\text{ rad}$$

Calculate the arc length $AC$ with radius $r = AD = 5\text{ cm}$:
$$\text{Arc } AC = r\theta = 5 \times 2.21429 \approx 11.0715\text{ cm}$$

Find the length of chord $AC$ using the Pythagorean theorem in right-angled triangle $ABC$:
$$AC = \sqrt{AB^2 + BC^2} = \sqrt{8^2 + 4^2} = \sqrt{64 + 16} = \sqrt{80} \approx 8.9443\text{ cm}$$

Calculate the total perimeter of the shaded segment:
$$\text{Perimeter} = \text{Arc } AC + \text{Chord } AC = 11.0715 + 8.9443 \approx 20.0\text{ cm}$$

ai_rubric.Circular Measure - Angle in Radians: Finds $\angle BDC = \arctan(4/3) \approx 0.9273$ rad and sector angle $\angle ADC = \pi - 0.9273 \approx 2.214$ rad.
ai_rubric.Calculating Perimeters: Calculates arc length $s = 5 \times 2.214 \approx 11.07$ cm and chord length $AC = \sqrt{80} \approx 8.944$ cm, summing to get perimeter $20.0$ cm.

skill_tags: Finding Areas of Composite Circular Regions

hints: The shaded region is a circular segment formed by subtracting the area of triangle $ADC$ from the area of sector $DAC$.
Calculate the area of sector $DAC$ using $\text{Area} = \frac{1}{2} r^2 \theta$ with $r = 5$ and $\theta \approx 2.214$ rad.
Calculate the area of triangle $ADC$ using base $AD = 5$ and perpendicular height $BC = 4$: $\text{Area} = \frac{1}{2} \times 5 \times 4$.
Subtract the area of triangle $ADC$ from the area of sector $DAC$ to find the shaded area.
walkthrough:
Calculate the area of sector $DAC$ using $r = 5\text{ cm}$ and $\theta = 2.21429\text{ rad}$:
$$\text{Area of Sector } DAC = \frac{1}{2} r^2 \theta = \frac{1}{2}(5^2)(2.21429) = \frac{25}{2}(2.21429) \approx 27.6786\text{ cm}^2$$

Calculate the area of triangle $ADC$ using base $AD = 5\text{ cm}$ and perpendicular height $BC = 4\text{ cm}$:
$$\text{Area of } \triangle ADC = \frac{1}{2} \times \text{base} \times \text{height} = \frac{1}{2} \times 5 \times 4 = 10\text{ cm}^2$$

Subtract the triangle area from the sector area to determine the area of the shaded region:
$$\text{Shaded Area} = \text{Area of Sector } DAC - \text{Area of } \triangle ADC = 27.6786 - 10 \approx 17.7\text{ cm}^2$$

ai_rubric.Finding Areas of Composite Circular Regi: Finds triangle area $\frac{1}{2}(5)(4) = 10\text{ cm}^2$ and subtracts to obtain shaded area $17.7\text{ cm}^2$.
